title: Lior and the Horizon
premise: Gideon Reyes, estranged child of archaeologist Dr. Elena Voss, has spent years drifting from dig site to dig site, refusing to stay anywhere long enough to be hurt again. When Elena's expedition up the Sereno River goes silent, Gideon joins a rescue party led by the expedition's disgraced financier, Marcus Hale, whose motives are anything but pure. In the high valley beyond the Cordillera del Viento, Gideon discovers Elena has found a tomb whose artifacts confer devastating political power on whoever claims them — and that Hale intends to seize them, with Elena as collateral. Crossing the range ahead of the snows with a small loyal band, Gideon must choose between exposing Hale's crimes through channels that will destroy their mother's legacy, or burying the truth with the tomb. In the end, Gideon chooses justice outside the law: the artifacts are returned to the valley's descendants, Hale is left to the mountain's mercy, and Gideon — for the first time — stops moving.
about_author: Paloma Amberdale is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain corridors before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who run from their pasts and the landscapes that refuse to let them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Working a salvage dig in a coastal town, Gideon is offered a permanent position — and declines it within the hour, packing before dawn. A letter from Elena Voss arrives, the first in three years. Emotional beat: the ache of a person who has made flight into an identity.

chapters.title: Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The letter contains Elena's last transmission coordinates and a plea disguised as small talk. Then a second message: the expedition's radio has gone dark for eleven days. Gideon tells themselves they're going for the artifact money, not the mother. Emotional beat: denial wearing the mask of practicality.

chapters.title: A Man Who Buys Rescues
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the river port of Puerto Cobre, Gideon meets Marcus Hale, the expedition's financier, who is outfitting a rescue with suspicious speed and too many armed men. Hale offers Gideon a generous wage and a lie about Elena's condition. Emotional beat: the first wrong note in a polished performance.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with interludes from boat pilot Sef Maren. The journey up the Sereno is a gauntlet of rapids, rotting checkpoints, and Hale's men testing Gideon's loyalties. Sef warns Gideon that Hale's last expedition came back short two people and long on silence. Emotional beat: unease hardening into watchfulness.

chapters.title: The Burned Camp
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They find the expedition's lower camp burned, supplies looted, and a radio smashed — but the destruction is days old and deliberate. Gideon reads the ground like a dig: this was staged. Someone wanted the world to believe the expedition dead. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by the thrill of the puzzle.

chapters.title: What the Porter Knew
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A wounded porter, left behind by Hale's advance team, reveals Elena's expedition is alive — held at the high valley by men Hale hired months ago. The 'rescue' is a retrieval operation. Sef must decide whether to tell Gideon and fracture the party. Emotional beat: loyalty to a stranger outweighing self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Turn at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Confronted with Sef's evidence, Gideon plays along with Hale, buying time while secretly planning to split off. Hale, sharper than expected, begins watching Gideon. A night patrol nearly catches them passing notes. Emotional beat: the exhausting double life of a liar telling the truth.

chapters.title: Foot of the Range
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The party reaches the Cordillera's foothills as the dry season's last weeks burn away. Gideon and Sef slip away at night with the porter and a stolen map, while Hale's men discover the betrayal and give chase. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration in equal measure — running toward, for once, instead of away.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The high pass is a maze of wind-carved spires where the map fails. One of Hale's trackers catches up; in the fight, the porter is badly hurt, forcing an impossible pace-or-mercy choice. Emotional beat: Gideon learns that stopping, this once, costs less than leaving.

chapters.title: Valley of the Second Sun
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They descend into the hidden valley and find the descendants of the tomb's builders — a community that has guarded the site for centuries and now shelters them. Gideon sees Elena's expedition held in the old mission compound. Emotional beat: awe undercut by the sight of a mother through a barred window.

chapters.title: Reunion, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena narrates her captivity and the tomb's discovery — artifacts that would let a government legitimize a land grab, or a resistance delegitimize a state. Gideon reaches her briefly through a drainage culvert; their first words in three years are an argument. Emotional beat: love that has forgotten its own language.

chapters.title: The Archive in the Stone
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The valley's elder, Ama Quispe, shows Gideon the tomb's true nature: not treasure but a record — proof of a treaty that makes Hale's employers' claims void. Hale doesn't want artifacts; he wants the evidence erased. Emotional beat: the shift from rescue to cause.

chapters.title: Snows on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The first storm closes the pass early; the escape window shrinks to days. Hale, desperate, tightens his grip on the compound and executes a prisoner as a warning. Sef scouts a route no map shows — the old salt road. Emotional beat: the clock becoming the true antagonist.

chapters.title: A Bargain with Thieves
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon offers Hale a trade: safe passage out for Elena and the expedition staff. Hale counters by demanding the treaty record itself. Gideon pretends to consider, buying a night, and hates how easily the corruption of power speaks their language. Emotional beat: the seduction of the deal that solves everything and costs the soul.

chapters.title: The Night of Two Fires
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The plan ignites: a decoy fire in the mission, the compound gates cut, prisoners moving toward the salt road under storm cover. It half-works — Elena is freed, but Sef is captured covering the retreat. Emotional beat: victory with a hole torn in it.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. On the salt road, Elena and Gideon finally speak honestly — about the dig that broke the family, the parent who chose a site over a child. Elena admits she stayed silent about Hale's funding for years. Emotional beat: truth offered as the only currency left between them.

chapters.title: Hale's Ascent
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale, holding Sef, forces a parley on the ridge: the record for the pilot. He genuinely believes he's the reasonable one — that documents like the treaty belong to whoever can use them. Emotional beat: the banality of a corrupt man's self-image.

chapters.title: The Exchange on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The exchange goes wrong by design: Gideon hands over a forged record, and when Hale's scholar exposes it, violence erupts on the storm-lashed ridge. Sef is freed; the treaty record's hiding place is compromised; the snows arrive early. Emotional beat: the moment cleverness runs out and only courage remains.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The party, Hale, and his men are trapped together above the tree line as the storm closes. Ama Quispe's people arrive to claim the record and their dead. Gideon must decide Hale's fate — the mountain's justice or a trial that would bury the valley's secret in courts for a decade. Emotional beat: power in its rawest form, and the temptation to misuse it.

chapters.title: The Mountain Decides
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Gideon chooses neither execution nor silence: the record is given to the valley's descendants, and Hale is marched down to face the porters' families and the law they will build themselves. Some of Hale's men, offered a choice, stay in the valley. Emotional beat: justice as something handed down to the people it belongs to.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The long walk down the Sereno, past the burned camp, carrying the wounded and the dead home. Elena and Gideon plan a proper, honest excavation with the valley's consent — the first dig Gideon has ever wanted to stay for. Emotional beat: grief and hope traveling in the same boat.

chapters.title: Lior and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, one year later. The valley's treaty is public; the land grab has collapsed; the site is a shared stewardship. Gideon, offered a directorship in the capital, declines — and instead takes the local post, signing a lease, planting a garden. The horizon is no longer an exit. Emotional beat: the quiet radical act of staying.
